To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hypertension and hypertension therapy are associated with decreases in health status, as measured by the SF-36, QWB, and TTO scales.
hypertension is associated with lower scores on health status measures, and this association is independent of the number of medications taken.

(1) self-reported hypertension is associated with clinically meaningful reductions in health-related quality of live (HRQOL); (2) this association is not explained by the presence of other chronic conditions; and (3) this association is present even after controlling for the effects of other chronic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between self-reported hypertension status and health status measures.
the effects of health status measures on the health status of the population.
the effects of hypertension and hypertension drug therapies upon health status and the quality of life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are many different types of hypertension, and the treatment for each type of hypertension may differ.

the health status of individuals with hypertension is lower than those without hypertension, and that the lower health status in the former group is not due to the effects of antihypersensitive medications, but rather the disease itself.
hypertension is associated with a decrease in self-reported HRQOL.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

hypertension and its treatment are associated with clinically relevant reductions in self-reported quality of life, and that these reductions are not fully explained by the effects of other comorbidities or by the presence of symptoms of hypertension.
we have demonstrated that hypertension is associated with decreased health status in a community-dwelliing population.
there is no difference in HRQOL between hypertensive patients and normotensive patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a significant decrease in quality of life associated with hypertension.
hypertension and its treatment are associated with clinically significant decrements in HRQoL.
hypertension is a significant contributor to the burden of disease in our society, and the impact of hypertension on health status is substantial.
